chunks.text: 28-year-old female, Associate Professional or Technician, resident of Queenstown, Singapore.
General Anesthesia with Propofol, Fentanyl, and Vecuronium, maintained with Sevoflurane and Spontaneous Breathing

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good morning! I'm going to be your anesthesiologist for your laparoscopic appendectomy today. I'd like to go through a few questions to make sure everything goes smoothly for you. Can you start by telling me a bit about your medical history?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Sure, doctor. I have type 2 diabetes, which I manage with Metformin and lifestyle changes. I also take Lisinopril for blood pressure and was on low-dose Aspirin, but I stopped that a few days ago as instructed.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for that. I see you have a history of obesity, with a BMI of 28.5. How have you been managing with that? Any breathing difficulties or other issues related to it?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yeah, I do get a bit of shortness of breath when I walk fast or climb stairs, but it's not too bad. I don't need any medication for that, just trying to keep fit lah.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Understood. Now, regarding allergies, your records say 'no known allergies,' but I always like to double-check. Have you ever had any reactions to medications, especially antibiotics?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Oh, actually, I think I had a reaction to a different antibiotic before. Not Penicillin, but something else... I think it was a Cephalosporin. I had nausea and vomiting after taking it once.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for sharing that. It's important we note that. So, to confirm, you had nausea and vomiting with a Cephalosporin, and a rash with Penicillin. Is that correct?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Yes, exactly. The rash with Penicillin was a while back, and the Cephalosporin reaction was more recent, maybe a year ago.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Appreciate the details. Now, about your current medications: you're on Metformin once daily, Lisinopril once daily, and Aspirin was stopped. Are you taking any other medications or supplements?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, just those three. I stopped the Aspirin as per the surgeon's advice.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. And have you had any previous surgeries or anesthesia before?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, this is my first time. I'm a bit nervous, to be honest.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: It's completely normal to feel that way. We'll make sure you're comfortable and safe throughout. Now, just to confirm, when was your last meal or drink?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I had a light dinner around 8 PM last night and nothing since midnight. Just a sip of water this morning for my medications.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect, that fits within the NPO guidelines. Finally, how have you been functioning day-to-day? Any limitations in your activities?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I can do most things, but sometimes I get tired faster, especially if I walk too much. But I can still do my daily routine without too much trouble.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Thank you for all that information. We'll be using general anesthesia with Propofol, Fentanyl, and Vecuronium, and then maintain with Sevoflurane and spontaneous breathing. Given your allergies, we'll avoid Penicillin and Cephalosporins. Any questions for me?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: No, I think that's all. Thank you, doctor.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:00] induction propofol one hundred twenty milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:02] fentanyl twenty micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:04] vecuronium eight milligrams

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:06] tube in, grade one view

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:10] sevoflurane at one point five percent

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:20] mean arterial pressure seventy five, gave phenylephrine ten micrograms

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:40] fluids two thousand milliliters crystalloid administered

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: [08:50] heart rate eighty five, mean arterial pressure ninety

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Hi there, how are you feeling now after the surgery?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: I'm feeling a bit groggy, but okay. My tummy is sore, but I expected that.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: That's understandable. Can you tell me your pain level on a scale from 1 to 10?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Maybe around 4 or 5. It's manageable, but I can feel it when I move.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Alright, we'll make sure to manage your pain. Are you feeling any nausea or dizziness?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: A little bit nauseous, but not too bad. I haven't eaten anything yet, though.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Okay, we'll keep an eye on that. How's your breathing? Any discomfort or shortness of breath?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Breathing is fine. I'm a bit stuffy from the tube, but I can breathe okay.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Good. Do you remember anything from the surgery or when you were waking up?

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Not really. I remember going to sleep and then waking up here. No strange dreams or anything.

segments.speaker: PROVIDER
segments.text: Perfect. Since you have a higher BMI and diabetes, we'll monitor you closely for any complications, but so far everything looks good.

segments.speaker: PATIENT
segments.text: Thanks, doctor. I appreciate it. I'm just ready to go home and rest.
